title: Properties of Amine-Containing Ligands That Are Necessary for Visible-Light-Promoted Catalysis with Divalent Europium

list_of_rare_earth_compounds.compound_name: trinuclear europium(III) methoxide/hydroxide chloride complex of 1,4,7-triazacyclononane

material_class.structural_family: discrete methoxide- and hydroxide-bridged Eu3 cluster with three capping TACN ligands and terminal chlorides

synthesis.procedure: Ligand 9 (1,4,7-triazacyclononane) and EuCl2 were combined in dry methanol in a glovebox at a 10:1 ligand-to-metal ratio (ligand 31.1–38.2 mM, 10 equiv; EuCl2 3.11–3.82 mM, 1 equiv) and stirred to form an Eu(II)–ligand mixture. X-ray-quality crystals were then grown by vapor diffusion at cold temperature from a concentrated solution of EuCl2 and 9. The colorless crystals that formed over a long crystallization period were the oxidized Eu(III) cluster [EuIII3(CH3O)4(OH)(9)3Cl3]Cl rather than an Eu(II) complex. No isolated yield is reported.
synthesis.temperature: vapor diffusion at cold temperature; solution preparation temperature not stated
synthesis.vessel_or_method: dry glovebox for solution mixing; vapor diffusion of a concentrated methanolic solution
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: Clear colorless crystals of the oxidized trinuclear Eu(III) cluster were obtained by vapor diffusion at cold temperature from a concentrated EuCl2/9 solution; crystals oxidized during prolonged crystallization.

properties.summary: Optical data are for EuCl2 plus ligand 9 (TACN) in methanol, not for the isolated oxidized Eu(III) crystal. Mixtures absorb at about 340–353 nm with a tail into the visible region (to about 470 nm) and emit at 480 nm. From that emission and the ground-state potential, the authors calculate an excited-state potential of −2.3 V versus NHE. Catalytic benzyl chloride coupling with this ligand gave no product.
